Package index

Running an optimization

One generic for every algorithm. The kind of objective is handled separately, by as_objective(), so an algorithm is written once.

minimize()
Minimize a Function
maximize()
Maximize a Function
optimizer_result()
S7 Class for the Result of an Optimization

Smooth problems

Methods that use derivatives of the objective. They are fast when the objective is smooth, and they cannot certify a solution at a kink.

newton()
Newton's Method with a Modified Hessian
chebyshev()
Chebyshev's Third-Order Method
bfgs()
BFGS
lbfgs()
Limited-Memory BFGS
cg()
Nonlinear Conjugate Gradients
bb()
The Barzilai-Borwein Method
gd()
Gradient Descent

Noisy and large problems

Adam, which tolerates a gradient that points downhill only on average. It draws no minibatches of its own: an objective that resamples is a closure written by the caller, who defines what an observation is.

adam()
Adaptive Moment Estimation

Problems with a kink

Methods for objectives with kinks, at which a descent method reaches the solution without being able to certify it, because the subgradient that it evaluates does not become small. bundle() tests whether zero lies in the convex hull of its subgradients, prox_grad() handles the kink through a proximal operator, and nelder_mead() and compass() use no derivative.

bundle()
The Proximal Bundle Method
prox_grad()
Proximal Gradient Method
nelder_mead()
The Nelder-Mead Simplex Method
compass()
Pattern Search, With Coordinate or Random Polling

One parameter

A function of one variable, minimized without derivatives by bracketing the minimum and reducing the bracket.

brent()
Brent's Method in One Dimension

Searching before descending

A global search for problems on which the answer depends on the basin in which the run begins. Its result is meant to be passed to a local method, which finds the minimum.

sa()
Simulated Annealing With an Adaptive Step

Wrapping an optimizer

Both are themselves optimizers, so they combine with every method above and with each other. A multi-start reports the number of distinct optimal values reached from its starts; a chain runs its stages in order, each starting where the previous one finished.

multistart()
Run an Optimizer From Many Starting Points
chain()
Run Optimizers One After Another

Stopping rules

A criterion is an object that implements one generic, so a user-defined rule is treated like a shipped one. An optimizer rejects a rule that it cannot evaluate instead of accepting one that never fires.

criterion()
S7 Class for Convergence Criteria
crit_met()
Has the Stopping Rule Been Met?
crit_needs()

crit_grad()
Stop When the Gradient Is Small
crit_abs_obj()
Stop When the Objective Stops Moving (Absolute)
crit_rel_obj()
Stop When the Objective Stops Moving (Relative)
crit_abs_par()
Stop When the Parameters Stop Moving (Absolute)
crit_rel_par()
Stop When the Parameters Stop Moving (Relative)
crit_stationary()
Stop When the Method's Own Measure of Progress Is Small
crit_never()
The Rule That Never Fires
crit_any()
Stop When Any of Several Rules Fires
crit_all()
Stop Only When Every Rule Fires

Line searches

How far to go along a direction, once the direction is chosen. The nonmonotone search is the default of the Barzilai-Borwein method, whose step length is the method itself and which relies on steps that increase the objective.

line_search()
S7 Class for Line Searches
armijo()
Backtracking Line Search with the Armijo Condition
wolfe()
Line Search Satisfying the Strong Wolfe Conditions
nonmonotone()
Nonmonotone Backtracking

Starting values

A starter takes the place of the vector of starting values and is resolved on the unconstrained scale, so a single constant gives a sensible value for every kind of parameter and every draw lies inside its bounds.

starter()
S7 Class for a Starting-Value Generator
start_zeros()
Start From Zero on the Unconstrained Scale
start_runif()
Start From a Uniform Draw on the Unconstrained Scale
starting_values()
Produce a Vector of Starting Values
infer_npar()
How Many Parameters the Objective Takes

The objective

A function of the parameter vector. The generic is the extension point: a caller with another kind of objective registers one method and every algorithm accepts that objective.

as_objective()
Normalize an Objective for the Optimizers

Writing a new optimizer

The requirements on a new minimize() method, and the functions that help to meet them. check_optimizer() runs twelve checks on what an optimizer reports, and reports separately the gaps that it reaches on the test problems, since performance and correctness are different questions.
